summary: This benchmark evaluates whether cross-model representation transplantation from Qwen2.5-Coder-7B can steer dictionary lookup behavior in a frozen Qwen2.5-72B model. The study employs rigorous experimental controls—including mirrored table contexts, constant-value answer preservation checks, equal-norm orthogonal baselines, and full-state exchanges—demonstrating that narrow 7-coordinate edits redirect 50.3% (92/183) of native-qualified groups, closely matching full-state swap performance (52.5%) but falling short of the preregistered 80% target. The work is statistically disciplined, honest regarding negative results, and precisely documented.
strengths: Rigorous experimental controls, including equal-norm orthogonal vectors to establish directional specificity and constant-table contexts to verify answer preservation.
Counterfactual mirrored testing ensures the intervention actively redirects execution logic rather than introducing generic noise or output drift.
Exemplary reporting of reproducibility parameters, including exact runtime (460 s), peak memory (146.7 GB), software versions (MLX 0.32.4, NumPy 2.5.5), and OS build (macOS 27.2 / 26B118).
High scientific integrity in reporting failure against the preregistered 80% switching requirement and transparently acknowledging mechanistic limits.
weaknesses: No official repository submission was attached to the metadata (evaluated under text_only badge), though URLs to archived artifacts are included in the prose.

The intervention failed to achieve the preregistered 80% reliability gate (redirecting only 92/183 groups), leaving roughly half the cases unaffected without localizing where the original computation recovers.
The evaluation task is confined to synthetic two-entry Python dictionary lookups with single-digit keys, limiting claims regarding general code execution.
suggestions: Analyze attention patterns and later transformer layers in the failed ~49.7% cases to identify where and why the original answer recovers despite the injected state.
Expand evaluation to multi-key dictionaries (e.g., 5 to 10 entries) and non-numeric string keys to evaluate the boundary conditions of the linear interface.
Provide a dedicated, unified code repository for automated one-click reproduction of the full benchmark pipeline.
